title: Put a consultant's table on the plan's date

blocks.text: A pipeline operator (invented for this practice) hired a consultant to value a compressor upgrade for each year it could start. The consultant's table `{start year: value}` in $k gives each entry valued at the start of its own start year, "as if that year were today". The operator's planning model needs every entry on one date, the start of `plan_year`, at the yearly rate `rate`. Some tables include starts earlier than `plan_year` (for a re-plan of work already under way).
Write `to_plan_date(values_at_start, rate, plan_year)`, returning the table on the plan's date.
Say in one sentence what an entry valued "at its own start" is missing, then write the conversion as a formula. About four lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from rebase import to_plan_date

entries = {2030: 650, 2031: 650, 2033: 610}

print("to 2030 at 4%:", {y: round(v, 3) for y, v in to_plan_date(entries, 0.04, 2030).items()})
print("to 2028 at 4%:", {y: round(v, 3) for y, v in to_plan_date(entries, 0.04, 2028).items()})
print("to 2032 at 4%:", {y: round(v, 3) for y, v in to_plan_date(entries, 0.04, 2032).items()})

cases.says: an entry valued at its own start year is discounted back to the plan's date, so equal entries become smaller for later starts
when the plan's date is earlier than every start, even the earliest entry is discounted
an entry for a start earlier than the plan's date is compounded forward to it

origin.section: Discount Every Start to One Valuation Date

concepts: every entry of a start-year table is valued on the model's single valuation date
